_about: The Codex builds RAVIS has pinned (runbook §2.2 invariant 6; RAVIS.md §15.1.2). A binary is a tested build only when its sha256 and both schema-tree hashes match one entry here. strict_rules_proven stays false until calibration proves the file rules on that exact binary, and until then new Codex work stays paused (untested_version). used_methods and strict_rules_surface are what RAVIS depends on in a new build (acceptance checks 5 and 7a); each entry's definitions file holds its experimental schema's per-definition hashes (ravis/codex/schema_report.py).
_file_rules_profile_about: The clarvis_run permission profile's -c flags (design §4.9), written at calibration once Codex's own validation errors fix their TOML syntax: {"name": "clarvis_run", "flags": ["-c", "…"]}, where a flag may name {user_home}, {ravis_config}, {codex_home} and {reproof_decoys}. null until then: the Codex process starts without it, and the file-rules re-test refuses to start.

tested.evidence: Measured for RAVIS R1 from /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex/0.154.0/bin/codex, reached through the Homebrew link /opt/homebrew/bin/codex: signed by Apple team 2DC432GLL2, prints codex-cli 0.154.0, and both schema trees were generated in a throwaway Codex home under a sandbox denying network access and every write outside that home. The stable tree equals the reference recorded for ChatGPT.app's 0.154.0-alpha.6.2. Calibration proves the file rules (STATUS.md, Codex engine build plan). The definition hashes (R2) were built from the protocol brief's generated experimental tree, whose tree hash equals this entry's experimental_tree.
